title: Code-space recovery for sample-based quantum diagonalization beyond native symmetry constraints
authors: Byeongyong Park, Sanha Kang, Doyeol Ahn, Keunhong Jeong
abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) diagonalizes a Hamiltonian in a compact subspace built from quantum samples, and its performance often relies on recovery procedures that exploit native constraints such as particle-number symmetry. For a broad class of eigenvalue problems, however, no analogous constraint is guaranteed, limiting the applicability of SQD-type recovery. Here, we introduce code-space recovery, which engineers recoverable structure through encoding rather than assuming it in the target problem. Using a dual-rail representation, each logical qubit is mapped to a physical pair, $|0\rangle \to |01\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \to |10\rangle$, making code-space violations in noisy samples detectable and repairable. We combine this encoding with self-consistent recovery and benchmark it on transverse- and mixed-field Ising models with up to 36 spin sites. Despite increased circuit overhead, code-space recovery yields lower projected Ritz energies than unencoded sample-support diagonalization even at smaller projected-basis dimensions, suggesting that engineered recoverable structure can extend SQD beyond native constraints.
summary: The paper presents code-space recovery as an advanced technique to enhance Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) for finding ground states of general quantum Hamiltonians. By employing a dual-rail encoding, the method engineers robustness against sampling errors, allowing accurate diagonalization even when natural symmetries are absent. This significantly extends the applicability and reliability of quantum simulation algorithms.
main_problem: To improve Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) for finding ground states of Hamiltonians when native symmetries are not guaranteed.
main_result: Code-space recovery, which engineers structure via dual-rail encoding and self-consistent repair, yields lower projected Ritz energies than unencoded methods even with increased circuit overhead.
method: The authors introduce code-space recovery using a dual-rail representation to encode logical qubits into physical pairs. This allows for the detection and iterative repair of sampling errors (code-space violations) during the diagonalization process.
model_or_system: The method is benchmarked on Ising-type spin Hamiltonians, specifically Transverse-Field and Mixed-Field Ising Models, up to 36 spin sites. The target operator $O$ is set to the Hamiltonian itself.
key_observables: Projected Ritz energies (estimating ground state energy), detection/repair of code-space violations, and comparison against classical reference energies from DMRG calculations.
important_parameters: The encoding doubles the qubit count; recovery involves iterative steps ($N_{I,max}$); benchmarks test varying projected basis dimensions ($D_{	ext{tar}}$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that engineered recoverable structure can compensate for the increased circuit overhead associated with the dual-rail encoding.
figures_summary: Figure 1 summarizes the workflow: combining dual-rail encoding with self-consistent code-space recovery to estimate the lowest Ritz pair of $O$.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the dual-rail encoding and the iterative, self-consistent code-space recovery algorithm (including clustering and stochastic repair), benchmarks this against unencoded methods on various Ising models, and validates results using classical reference energies.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses limitations in applying quantum simulation techniques to complex Hamiltonians by providing a robust error mitigation strategy that moves beyond relying solely on inherent physical symmetries.

figures.caption: Fig. 1 SQD workflow combining dual-rail encoding with self-consistent code-space recovery. The objective of this workflow is to estimate the lowest Ritz pair of a target Hermitian operator O. (1) Each logical qubit is encoded as |0⟩7→|01⟩and |1⟩7→|10⟩, and each logical operator A used in the sampling circuits is mapped to an encoded operator A′ satisfying A′V = V A, where V is the encoding isometry. The encoding constrains every physical qubit pair to have Hamming weight one, making code-space violations detectable and providing structural information for subsequent recovery. Fig. 3 Energy-variance extrapolation for 25-spin-site recovered states. Projected Ritz energy is plotted against energy variance for states obtained from recovered bases constructed by code-space recovery on encoded hardware samples. Results are shown for (a) 1D TFIM, (b) 1D MFIM, and (c) 5 × 5 2D TFIM. Each point denotes one projected Ritz state, and the color indicates the realized projected dimension. Red lines denote linear fits to all displayed energy-variance sweep points from Dtar = 1.5 × 106 to 2.5 × 106, and dashed horizontal lines indicate the exact reference energy for 1D TFIM and DMRG reference energies for 1D MFIM and 2D TFIM.
